marks.gloss_en: שנאמר: מה לי ולך מלך יהודה לא עליך אתה היום -- Neco declared he did not come against Josiah

'and he sent messengers to him saying: what have I to do with you, king of Judah? not against you this day, but against the house of my war... refrain from the god who is with me, lest he destroy you' (2 Chr 35:21)
what is 'the god who is with me'? Rav Yehuda said in Rav's name: this is idolatry
'and the archers shot at King Josiah... for I am sorely wounded' (2 Chr 35:23) -- what is 'sorely wounded'? Rav Yehuda said in Rav's name: it teaches that they made his whole body like a sieve
why was Josiah punished? because he should have consulted Jeremiah and did not
(entertained) what 'sword' [in 'and a sword shall not pass through your land', Lev 26:6]? if you say a sword that is not of peace
Jeremiah [seeing his lips move] said: perhaps, Heaven forbid, he is saying something improper because of his pain
for every trouble that may [lit. should not] come upon the community they sound the alarm for it
תא שמע, דתניא: ... רבי חנן בן פיטום ... משום רבי עקיבא אומר: אין מתריעין על הדבר כל עיקר -- the baraita has a tanna who allows no alarm for pestilence at all
they sound the alarm for pestilence on Shabbat
side one of the iba'ya: the Sages did not concede to Shimon HaTimni on Shabbat, but on a weekday they conceded -- one sounds the alarm for pestilence on a weekday
תניא נמי הכי: in a year of abundant rain the mishmar asks the ma'amad to pray for the brothers in the Diaspora, that their houses not be their graves
Rami bar Rav Yud: and in the Diaspora they sound the alarm for it [an excess of rain]
והתניא: ידיו! -- a baraita reports R' Eliezer's measure as dipping the hands, not the feet
רגליו כידיו קאמינא -- 'his feet like his hands' is what I meant (unattributed; phrased in R' Eliezer's first person)
until where must rain fall that they pray it not fall? R' Eliezer: so that a man may stand at Keren Ofel and dip his feet in the water
R' Yochanan: from where that one does not pray over an excess of good? as it says 'bring the whole tithe into the storehouse...' (Mal 3:10)
Rabba bar bar Chana: I myself saw Keren Ofel, and an Arab standing there riding a camel with a spear in his hand looked like a worm
'and I will give your rains in their season' (Lev 26:4): [the land] neither drunk nor thirsty, but moderate
תא שמע: כמלא פי תנור -- the mishnah says the MOUTH of an oven
(asked) like the cover of the oven?
(the mishnah, cited) an incident: Elders went down from Jerusalem to their cities [and decreed a fast]...
for a city that gentiles surrounded they sound the alarm on Shabbat
R' Yosei: an individual may not afflict himself by fasting
an incident: wolves swallowed two children and excreted them
